note:
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Runny nose, nasal congestion, and cough.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a pediatric patient brought in by guardian with upper respiratory symptoms that began approximately 12-24 hours ago around supper time. Symptoms include rhinorrhea with clear nasal discharge, nasal congestion, non-barky cough, ear pulling, and nasal rubbing. Rectal temperature measured at 100.3°F this morning. Appetite has decreased - patient consumed approximately 7 ounces from bottle this morning and barely finished second bottle, refused cereal. Guardian notes patient is irritable and energetic but having difficulty sleeping, fighting sleep. Possible exposures include older sister currently symptomatic with similar illness and recent playdate with nephew who was later found to have sinus infection. Home management attempted includes saline nasal mist, acetaminophen given this morning when child felt warm/diaphoretic despite home air conditioning, baby Vick's applied to feet, and humidifier use.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Constitutional: Irritable, energetic, sleep disturbance
HEENT: Clear rhinorrhea, nasal congestion, ear pulling, nasal rubbing, non-barky cough
Fever: 100.3°F rectal
GI: Decreased appetite, refusing solid foods
All other systems reviewed and unremarkable.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Cradle cap with recent worsening

MEDICATIONS
- Acetaminophen (Tylenol) - given this morning
- Saline nasal mist
- Baby Vick's

ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.

FAMILY HISTORY
Older sister currently ill with upper respiratory infection symptoms
Nephew with recent sinus infection

SOCIAL HISTORY
Participates in family playdates.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: Alert, tolerating examination well
HEENT: Ears normal on otoscopy; cradle cap visible on scalp
Lungs: Clear to auscultation bilaterally with excellent respiratory effort

RESULTS
Rectal temperature: 100.3°F

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Viral upper respiratory infection:
   - Early viral presentation; monitor for progression to bacterial superinfection
   - Continue hydration and rest
   - Monitor closely for development of barking/croupy cough
   - Provided prescription for croup medication at half-teaspoon dose (adjusted for patient weight); use only if barky cough develops; treat for 5 days if needed
   - Medication given now to have available over weekend as fallback if symptoms worsen
   - No antibiotics indicated at this time
   - For nonproductive cough, may use Zarbee's cough syrup at infant dosing
   - Educated guardian: No honey or honey-containing products (e.g., Honey Nut Cheerios) due to botulism risk in infants; agave nectar is safe alternative
   - No COVID-19 detected

2. Cradle cap (seborrheic dermatitis):
   - Initiate antifungal/anti-dandruff shampoo: Head & Shoulders, Selsun Blue, or Nizoral AD (regular strength only, not extra strength)
   - Use twice weekly, not daily; continue regular shampoo on other wash days
   - Continue soft brush and baby oil to remove scale
   - Avoid shampoo contact with eyes during rinsing
   - Expected improvement within 6 weeks
   - Contact office if worsens

3. Follow-up: Appointments scheduled for patient and older sister in 1 week.
